entities.summary: Ray Shirley White Sr. is an African American soul vocalist and rock and blues guitarist, best known as a member of Frank Zappa's touring ensembles. He was drafted into Zappa's band in late 1976, being featured on rhythm guitar and vocals, forming a vocal harmony partnership with Ike Willis on later tours in 1980 and 1984. White's vocals can be heard on Zappa in New York and You Are What You Is as well as others. White can also be found on a The Torture Never Stops and Does Humor Belong in Music?; the former is a DVD from Zappa's 1981 tour and the latter filmed at the pier in New York in 1984; the video features White and Ike Willis' vocal harmonies.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a member of Frank Zappa's touring ensembles, Ray White contributed to several influential albums and performances in the late 1970s and early 1980s, shaping the sound of progressive rock and blues. His work with Zappa had a lasting impact on the music industry.
